independent_checks.py randomly sampled 990 finite integer-window patterns for chromatic bound
correctness.rationale: The integer intervals I_n form a perfect interval-intersection graph and can be greedily colored using at most maximum point overlap Delta. For a color with ordered endpoints n_j, nonoverlap implies n_(j-1)<=n_j-K_(n_j), so the centered Z_(n_j) are bounded martingale differences for the coarse filtration; conditional Hoeffding gives E exp(lambda S_c)<=exp(2lambda² r_c) for |Z|<=2. Generalized Holder with p_c=(sum sqrt r_d)/sqrt r_c and sum 1/p_c=1 yields exp(2lambda² (sum sqrt r_c)^2). Optimizing Chernoff yields two-sided 2exp(-x²/(8 R)); Cauchy–Schwarz gives R<=Delta N. Set x=epsilon N to obtain convergence in probability if Delta_N=o(N). Independent randomized checks on 990 integer-horizon patterns confirmed interval-coloring equals max overlap and the Holder variance proxy inequality. No independence of the Y_n or random horizon assumptions are smuggled in.
residual_risks: All horizons deterministic and chosen independently of data; stopping-time/adaptive horizons are outside the proof.

originality.rationale: Vovk (2025/2026) proved a common K fixed-horizon centered forecast LLN using residue classes; that theorem does not directly handle arbitrary deterministic changing K_n, especially one horizon of order N amid mostly K_n=1. Coloring actual backward information intervals and bounding by maximum simultaneous overlap is the added conditional concentration result. Ordinary interval graph perfection and Hoeffding/Hölder are classical ingredients, so general dependent-sequence inequalities remain a potential implicit-coverage risk.
residual_risks: An existing general dependent-martingale coloring inequality may imply the current bound as a corollary, although no decisive covering theorem was identified.
The new contribution is a motivated nonuniform forecasting corollary of elementary tools, not novelty of Hoeffding, Holder or interval graph coloring.
